item.title: Oil Prices Rise After Hormuz Tanker Attack, Houthi Claims Stoke Supply Fears
item.description: Oil prices rose more than 2% after an attack on a tanker transiting Hormuz and Houthi militants claimed to have struck Saudi energy infrastructure again.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of October 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: Chinese Executive Close to Nvidia CEO Suspected of Giving China Information
item.description: Investigators believed the woman, Alice Huang, was recruited based on her relationship with Jensen Huang.

item.title: Ukraine Hits Russian Oil Refinery, Ending Pause and Defying Trump
item.description: The strike ends a two-week halt in refinery attacks that came amid pressure from the U.S. to halt such operations.

item.title: BOE Survey Points to Faster Price Rises, But Slowing Wage Growth
item.description: Businesses expected the prices they charge to rise by 3.8% over the coming 12 months, an increase from the 3.7% expected in September.

item.title: Inside the U.S. Military’s Open-Ended Mission to Keep Gulf Oil Flowing
item.description: ​The near-daily missions to protect ships have allowed the U.S. to hold the line in a conflict that has dragged on since February and threatened access to the world’s oil supplies.

item.title: The Troubled History of Russia’s Antiplague Institute
item.description: The Siberian lab where a biologist recently died of a mysterious pneumonia has been cited multiple times for safety violations.

item.title: Ukraine Pauses Strikes on Russian Refineries After Pressure From U.S.
item.description: Kyiv has temporarily halted one of its most effective operations against Moscow after complaints from President Trump.

item.title: Machado’s Return Offers a Preview of Venezuela’s Next Election—Whenever It Comes
item.description: Interim President Rodríguez and opposition leader Machado laid out competing visions, sounding the opening gun of a power struggle.

item.title: Why Does Spain Keep Having Deadly Rail Accidents?
item.description: With elections around the corner, rail safety has become a campaign issue in the wake of Wednesday’s deadly crash.

item.title: Top Military Admiral Briefs Trump on Iran Options
item.description: A White House meeting included a rare in-person briefing by Adm. Brad Cooper, as the U.S. weighs new combat operations.

item.title: Trump’s Deportation Deal With Cameroon Will Equip Unit Accused of War Crimes
item.description: The Trump administration agreed to send armored personnel carriers to Cameroon as part of a deal under which the country is accepting deportees from third countries.

item.title: Oil Prices Ease as U.S. Seeks to Renew Diplomacy With Iran
item.description: Oil prices fell as traders assessed fresh U.S. efforts to revive peace negotiations with Iran, while persistent Middle East supply risks and the possibility of renewed military escalation limited losses.

item.title: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas, Leftist Leader Who Paved Mexico’s Path to Democracy, Dies at 92
item.description: His disputed 1988 presidential bid challenged the PRI’s decades-long grip on power and helped open Mexico’s political system to competition.

item.title: Cleveland-Cliffs to Retain Stelco Amid Jobs Dispute With Canadian Government
item.description: Cleveland-Cliffs is ruling out selling Stelco until the business improves production and 175 laid-off workers return to their jobs, an effort Chief Executive Lourenco Goncalves said hinges on Canadians buying the company’s steel products.

item.title: Israel’s Arabs Emerge as Key Political Powerhouse
item.description: Arab parties won one in six seats, emerging as potential kingmakers amid Netanyahu’s fraud allegations.

item.title: Christine Lagarde to Resign Early as ECB President
item.description: Europe’s largest countries are already jockeying over who will succeed Lagarde—and inherit responsibility for an economy facing mounting problems.

item.title: China’s Xi Demands More Loyalty as Purges Trim Party Elite
item.description: The Chinese leader is tightening his grip on the Communist Party with relentless purges and new strictures on discipline.

item.title: Irish Economy Surges Again in Boost to Eurozone
item.description: The growth is pushing hopes for a continued expansion across the eurozone as a whole, despite higher energy costs.

item.title: As Missile Stockpiles Dwindle and China Looms, U.S. Turns to Japan for Production
item.description: Tokyo and Washington agreed to establish a facility in Japan to assemble key air-to-air missiles.
